title: Generative AI and Emerging Financial Crime Typologies
summary: How criminals use generative AI for synthetic identities, deepfake onboarding and large-scale social engineering, and the resilience firms and supervisors need to build.
topic: Reducing Financial Crime & Delivering Market Integrity
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How criminals use generative AI for synthetic identities, deepfake onboarding and large-scale social engineering, and the resilience firms and supervisors need to build.
Learning Objectives: Recognise financial crime typologies enabled by generative AI
Assess firms' identity verification and liveness controls
Challenge firms' resilience against AI-enabled social engineering
Syllabus: Synthetic identity fraud and deepfake-enabled onboarding
Voice cloning, deepfake video and AI-generated phishing
Liveness detection, multi-factor verification and their limits
Case study: a firm targeted by a deepfake-enabled fraud
Intended Audience: AML/CFT, sanctions and financial crime supervisors and inspectors
Market surveillance, conduct and data analytics staff working on financial crime risk
Senior managers shaping the authority's financial crime strategy and use of SupTech
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT, sanctions or conduct supervision is helpful. No technical background in AI or data science is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
